chunks.arabic_text: ١٥ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ، أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ، الْهَمْدَانِيُّ، مَوْلَاهُمْ - هَذَا أَصَحُّ مَا يُنْتَسَبُ إِلَيْهِ -.

translations.en: 15 – Muḥammad b. Sinān, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Hamdānī, their client – this is the most correct of what he is related to.

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفٌ، غَالٍ، يَضَعُ (الْحَدِيثَ) لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: Weak, a ghālī, he fabricates (ḥadīth). He is not turned to.

en.summary: Muḥammad ibn Sinān al-Hamdānī is identified as the most authentic possessor of this name, yet he is classified among the *du'afā'* (weak narrators) for being a *ghālī* (exaggerator, often associated with the Ghulat sect) who fabricated hadith. His status as unreliable is emphasized by the phrase 'not relied upon,' reflecting the critical scrutiny applied to him in Shia hadith sciences due to his doctrinal deviations and tendency toward fabrication.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hamdani is and his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences.

key_terms.غَالٍ: Exaggerator (specifically in theological beliefs, often Shi'i)
key_terms.يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: He is turned to / relied upon
